page: Amazon Web Services r6a.32xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by AMD EPYC 7R13 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this server features 128 virtual CPUs consisting of 64 physical cores with 2 threads per core running at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. It is equipped with 1024.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance utilizes the AWS Nitro hypervisor and offers 50 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth.

In benchmark evaluations, the r6a.32xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU and memory performance. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test and Passmark CPU score both rank in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory performance is a key strength, with small-block read-only memory bandwidth achieving top-tier status, and large-block read and write bandwidths placing in the top 25%. Database operations, such as Redis SET operations, also achieve top-tier performance, processing 136.38 million operations per second.

While the instance delivers high memory capacity and strong computational throughput, it lacks local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware. This requires reliance on network-attached storage for persistent data, which may impact I/O-intensive workloads compared to instances with local NVMe. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r6a.32xlarge provides high memory density and massive parallel processing capabilities on a mature DDR4 platform, offering a balanced cost-to-resource ratio for memory-bound workloads without the premium of newer DDR5 architectures.

The hardware profile and benchmark results make the r6a.32xlarge highly suitable for memory-intensive applications. Recommended workloads include large-scale in-memory databases like Redis, enterprise-grade relational databases, big data analytics, and high-throughput web serving. It is also well-suited for memory-bound scientific simulations and software compilation tasks.
